clips.text_zh: 又遲到。望住BTC升15%先嚟講點解唔買，我係咪應該寫低自己個名？patience = 0。命理都救唔到我
clips.text_en_b1: You watch BTC do nothing for weeks and ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened?
clips.text_en_b2: You watch Bitcoin do absolutely nothing for weeks, so you ignore it and lose interest. Then, almost on cue, the price jumps by 15%, and suddenly everyone wants to get in. Why is it that people only develop an appetite for risk after the market has already moved? At this point, writing my name on a list of people who always arrive late might be appropriate, because my patience with these cycles is already zero.
clips.text_en_c1: One can scarcely ignore Bitcoin for weeks on end, dismissing it as a stagnant asset, and then suddenly feel compelled to buy once it has already appreciated by fifteen percent. The pattern is infuriating in its predictability: the moment a substantial move materialises, retail interest surges as if on cue. Anyone who failed to position themselves beforehand is now scrambling to chase momentum that, by definition, has already occurred. The irony, of course, is that those who exercise patience are typically vindicated, whereas those who capitulate at the top invariably buy precisely when conviction should be lowest. Discipline, evidently, remains an undervalued commodity in this market cycle.
clips.text_en_c2: One is perpetually late to the party, and the irony is almost too on the nose to bear. Bitcoin idles in purgatory for weeks on end, drawing precisely nothing from the crowd, until—almost as if on cue—it rips fifteen percent in a single motion, at which point every procrastinator suddenly discovers an insatiable appetite for entry. The question, then, is not why people buy the breakout, because that impulse is as old as markets themselves, but rather why conviction evaporates so completely during the consolidation phase that precedes it. Patience, evidently, is a virtue the retail cohort cannot afford; even the most generous astrological counsel cannot rescue those who possess the impeccable timing of a broken clock, late twice a day.

clips.text_zh: 200日SMA突破 + 4年周期 兩個unbreakable rule 即刻打架。底喺58k？咁個bear market得6個月，搞唔掂。prop firm個倉又再被chur
clips.text_en_b1: Two unbreakable crypto rules just broke at the same time. Rule 1: breaking the 1D 200 SMA after a bear market starts the next bull run. Rule 2: the 4-year cycle. If this is a new bull run, the bottom was 58k only two months ago. A 6-month bear market is too short.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on conflicting BTC cycle signals
clips.text_en_b2: Two supposedly unbreakable crypto rules have collided, and neither provides a convincing answer. Rule one claims that breaking the daily 200-day SMA marks the start of the next bull run, while rule two points to the familiar four-year cycle. If this really is a fresh bull market, the bottom was only around $58,000 two months ago. That would make the preceding bear market just six months long, which is too short to fit the established pattern, so the prop-firm position is getting hit again.
clips.text_en_c1: Two ostensibly ironclad technical principles have collided in rather spectacular fashion. The first axiom dictates that a daily candle closing above the 200-day simple moving average, following the conclusion of a bear market, heralds the onset of the subsequent bull cycle. The second invokes the cyclicality inherent to Bitcoin's roughly four-year halving rhythm. Were one to take both at face value, the conclusion would be deeply troubling: the cyclical bottom at fifty-eight thousand dollars occurred barely two months ago, which renders a six-month bear market implausibly brief. Such a compressed timeframe strains credulity, suggesting that one of these revered indicators may, in fact, be losing its predictive validity.
clips.text_en_c2: Two ostensibly ironclad axioms of crypto market structure have, within a matter of days, collided head-on in a manner that renders reconciliation difficult, if not impossible. The first holds that a daily-chart reclaim of the two-hundred-day simple moving average, occurring in the wake of a cyclical bear phase, constitutes the inaugural signal of the subsequent bull market. The second, more metaphysical in nature, insists upon the inviolability of the four-year halving cycle. Should the former interpretation prove correct, then the cyclical trough must be located somewhere in the vicinity of fifty-eight thousand dollars—a bottom set, distressingly, only two months prior. A six-month bear market is, by virtually any historical standard, an unconscionably abbreviated affair. The contradictions defy tidy synthesis, and proprietary trading desks now find their positioning throttled yet again.

clips.text_zh: 24/7 coding agents 一個月push 1000個PR。我喺度survey仲人手對數，AI真係連我份工都想搶。廢柴自救mode開返
clips.text_en_b1: She runs a bunch of AI coding agents 24/7 and pushes about 1000 PRs a month. Her method is based on trial and error, not on understanding how LLMs actually work. Still, the output is real. White-collar coding is changing fast.
clips.text_en_b2: She runs a group of AI coding agents around the clock, and the system pushes roughly 1,000 pull requests every month. Although her method may rely heavily on trial and error rather than a proper understanding of how large language models actually work, the results are undeniably real. Meanwhile, I am still doing manual reconciliation for a survey, which makes the warning signs impossible to ignore. AI does not seem satisfied with merely helping; it may be coming for my job as well.
clips.text_en_c1: She has reportedly deployed a constellation of AI coding agents operating continuously, which collectively dispatch approximately one thousand pull requests per month. Although her methodology rests primarily upon empirical iteration rather than any rigorous comprehension of how large language models actually function under the hood, the tangible output she generates is indisputably real. This development carries significant implications for white-collar software development, a sector whose contours are being reshaped at a pace that few anticipated even eighteen months ago. The traditional paradigm in which human engineers serve as the sole architects of production-grade code is being quietly but inexorably dismantled, and the profession's defenders would do well to take note.
clips.text_en_c2: A solo developer, having elected to outsource virtually the entirety of her cognitive labour, presently orchestrates a constellation of AI coding agents that operate on a continuous, round-the-clock basis, collectively marshalling in the neighbourhood of one thousand pull requests per calendar month. What renders the enterprise genuinely arresting is that her methodology, far from being grounded in any sophisticated theoretical understanding of large language model architecture, is instead the product of relentless empirical iteration—a process of trial and error of almost artisanal stubbornness. The output, however, is conspicuously real, and the implications for white-collar software work are not merely incremental but quietly tectonic. Those of us still manually reconciling spreadsheets might reasonably wonder whether the obsolescence clock has, in fact, already struck.

clips.text_zh: 連呢啲都有人討論。我淨係想返工、考牌、儲100K USD然後閃人返美國。香港真係好dirty同好逼
clips.text_en_b1: A /pol/ thread compiles cases across Singapore, Malaysia and Hong Kong where Indonesian maids had sex with underage boys, some as young as 3, 6 and 11. Several maids later falsely claimed the boys raped them. The thread links an archived report with the cases.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread compiling cases across SG, MY, HK
clips.text_en_b2: A /pol/ thread has gathered several disturbing cases reported across Singapore, Malaysia, and Hong Kong, all involving Indonesian maids and underage boys, including children aged three, six, and eleven. In a number of these cases, the maids later made false accusations that the boys had raped them, apparently turning the original incidents into a weapon. The thread links to an archived report containing the cases, although the original poster expresses frustration that this kind of material is even being discussed.
clips.text_en_c1: A thread on the fringe board compiles a series of disturbing cases drawn from Singapore, Malaysia, and Hong Kong, documenting incidents in which Indonesian domestic workers reportedly engaged in sexual relations with underage boys, some as young as three, six, and eleven. Several of the accused subsequently reversed their accounts, falsely claiming that the children in question had in fact raped them. The thread consolidates these accounts alongside an archived investigative report containing the underlying documentation. Whether the compilation constitutes genuine journalistic effort or merely opportunistic aggregation remains a matter of considerable interpretive dispute among those who have examined its contents.
clips.text_en_c2: A sprawling thread on /pol/, whose contents one would ordinarily dismiss as the fevered imagination of terminally online ideologues, has instead compiled a sobering catalogue of judicial cases spanning Singapore, Malaysia, and Hong Kong, each documenting instances in which Indonesian domestic workers became entangled in sexual encounters with minors—some as devastatingly young as three, six, and eleven years of age. The horror deepens considerably when one notes the subsequent reversals, in which a number of the accused maids inexplicably recanted their accounts and recast themselves as the wronged parties. The thread preserves links to archived regional reporting that substantiates each case. It is grim, evidentiary fare, and it starkly resists the comforts of summary dismissal.

clips.text_zh: S15睇visual就得lol。睇完BLG對T1我已經唔想講嘢，CFO幾時先唔再被人零封。Tommy都話唔睇今年
clips.text_en_b1: The visuals are nice and that is literally it, everything else sucks. The video itself has nice art direction but the story and gameplay fall flat. A common /v/ complaint when a new release only sells on style.
clips.text_en_b2: The visual design is attractive, but unfortunately that is pretty much the entire achievement. After watching BLG play T1, I have run out of things to say, because the presentation looks polished while the story and gameplay fall completely flat. The problem is not simply that the game is weak in several areas, but that it appears to rely on style as a substitute for substance. Even Tommy has said he is not watching this year, and I am starting to understand why.
clips.text_en_c1: The production values are genuinely commendable, and that observation, regrettably, constitutes the entirety of any praise one can extend. The visual direction demonstrates a sophisticated aesthetic sensibility, yet the narrative underpinning it feels conspicuously hollow, and the gameplay mechanics themselves fail to compensate for that vacuum. It is a recurring lament within enthusiast communities whenever a new release elects to trade substantive design for surface-level polish. Style, it seems, can effectively mask a multitude of structural deficiencies, at least until players progress beyond the opening hours and encounter the absence beneath the gloss.
clips.text_en_c2: Season 15, for those whose aesthetic sensibilities eclipse their threshold for narrative competence, offers a visual banquet of genuinely arresting quality—and, regrettably, precious little else. One emerges from extended viewings of marquee fixtures, such as the recent BLG versus T1 exhibition, possessing an abiding appreciation for art direction while registering a comprehensive failure of storytelling, mechanical depth, and competitive integrity. The critique, which has achieved near-consensus status across /v/, is by now woefully familiar: when a product's principal contribution to the medium lies in its surface presentation alone, the substance beneath inevitably registers as a profound betrayal. Even T1's own Tommy has publicly disavowed further engagement with the present competitive season.

clips.text_zh: 1.5k USD搞home gym。我而家連gym月費都覺得貴，但肥仔信成日push我話要繼續練。Squat rack + barbell + adjustable bench 就夠
clips.text_en_b1: I have $1,500 to spend on home gym equipment and cardio is already sorted. What would /fit/ buy to maximize gains? The thread suggests a squat rack, an Olympic barbell, weight plates and an adjustable bench as the core setup.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking how to spend $1.5K on a home gym
clips.text_en_b2: I have about $1,500 available to build a home gym, although I already find a normal monthly gym membership expensive, and cardio equipment is otherwise taken care of. Since the fat guy keeps pushing me to keep training, I would rather make a sensible one-off purchase than pay recurring fees. The main foundation should be a solid squat rack, a quality Olympic barbell, suitable weight plates, and an adjustable bench, because these items provide enough flexibility for serious strength training without turning the room into…
clips.text_en_c1: Operating with a modest budget of fifteen hundred dollars and having already addressed one's cardiovascular requirements through alternative means, the question becomes which foundational pieces of resistance-training equipment would maximise hypertrophy and strength progression. The prevailing consensus, drawing upon accumulated wisdom from experienced practitioners, gravitates toward a relatively constrained inventory: a sturdy squat rack capable of accommodating heavy loads, an Olympic-grade barbell of reputable manufacture, a sufficient quantity of calibrated weight plates, and an adjustable bench that permits variation in angles. This configuration, though minimalist, ostensibly provides the essential framework upon which a comprehensive home training regimen can be constructed.
clips.text_en_c2: Armed with a modest but not insignificant budget of fifteen hundred dollars earmarked exclusively for resistance apparatus—cardiovascular equipment having been satisfactorily resolved through alternative means—I have canvassed /fit/ in search of an optimal home-gym configuration predicated upon maximal hypertrophic return. While a persistently gym-averse friend, whose corpulent enthusiasm far outstrips his own adherence to any disciplined regimen, continues to insist upon the merits of continuity, the consensus that has emerged from the thread is both economical and unsentimental: a heavy-duty squat rack, an Olympic-specification barbell, a calibrated set of weight plates, and an adjustable bench comprise the irreducible foundation upon which any subsequent expansion may plausibly be constructed.

clips.text_zh: AI可以整睇得落嘅動畫slideshow。睇到Demon Slayer同Gundam 00嗰啲人手繪，我覺得AI做唔到我已經好嘅嘢。靠AI續命都嫌多餘
clips.text_en_b1: Chinese AI tools can now generate somewhat watchable anime slideshows. People are using them to adapt niche manga that would never get a real anime. The /a/ thread debates whether this kills studios or finally lets obscure manga get animated.
clips.text_en_b2: Chinese AI tools can now produce anime-style slideshows that are actually watchable, even though they may lack the fluid movement and careful craftsmanship of traditional animation. Fans are using them to adapt obscure manga that would probably never receive a proper television release, which has opened a fresh debate on /a/. Some argue that this could finally give neglected series a chance to be seen, while others worry that cheap, AI-generated productions may undermine professional studios.
clips.text_en_c1: Chinese-developed artificial intelligence tools have recently attained the capability of producing anime-style content that, while hardly indistinguishable from hand-drawn productions, achieves a threshold of watchability previously thought unattainable by automated means. Enthusiasts are leveraging these platforms to adapt obscure manga whose commercial viability would never justify commissioning a traditional studio. The discourse this provokes is sharply polarised: optimists contend that democratised production tools will finally illuminate neglected works, whereas pessimists counter that studios already marginalised by market dynamics will suffer further erosion. Watching craftsmen labour over productions such as Demon Slayer, one appreciates the irreplaceable value of human artisanship.
clips.text_en_c2: A clutch of newly emergent Chinese artificial intelligence tools has, somewhat to the dismay of purists, attained a threshold of visual coherence sufficient to render what one might charitably describe as anime—the better descriptor being 'animated slideshows,' though the distinction is admittedly academic at this point. Enthusiasts have eagerly deployed these systems to adapt marginal manga properties whose commercial prospects would, in any rational calculus, preclude the considerable expense of a traditional studio production. The resulting schism on /a/ is predictably polarising: techno-optimists celebrate the democratisation of adaptation, while traditionalists lament the instrumentalisation of a craft whose practitioners spent decades refining nuance that no diffusion model presently replicates. Demon Slayer and Gundam 00, rendered by hand, stand as inconvenient reminders of what is being algorithmically approximated.
